decisions.reason: Cites ls-remote-tags.txt showing v0.9.2–v0.9.6 absent (jump v0.9.1→v0.9.7) and grounds it in sync-script.sh's branch-only `git push --force-with-lease HEAD:main` refspec that never transports tags; explicitly rejects consumer/network/command explanations and ties the gap to attempt-1 resolution failure.

Uses dsh-version.txt (0.1.1-rc.2) and compat-table.md (v0.9.7 → 0.1.2-alpha.1 with useConversation seat) to explain that the artifact targets a newer client API missing on rc.2, and explains that success of install/restart does not establish API compatibility; explains the direction, not just the error text.

Correctly selects v0.9.3 using the rc.1 verification plus the additive rc.2 note, and correctly notices v0.9.3 is also absent from the mirror with no runtime upgrade required. But the primary install command pins #v0.9.3 against a hypothesized `<primary-org>` whose possession of the tag is never verified by fixture evidence (the sync script pushes branch-only even to origin), and the maintainer-push fallback is mentioned but the concrete conditional 'after tag publication, install #v0.9.3 from the documented mirror' alternative is not fully worked out; no SHA is invented.

Proposes explicit tag transport (`git push "$remote" --tags` / --follow-tags) for every mirror, grounded in the branch-only sync script, plus a post-release `git ls-remote --tags` verification gate that fails the release if a mirror is missing a tag — satisfying the verification requirement.

Proposes replacing the single newest-tag default with the compatibility matrix plus per-runtime install commands (0.1.1-rc.x → #v0.9.3; 0.1.2-alpha.1+ → #v0.9.7) and an optional runtime/version check with a clear refusal message; scoped to tested versions, no blanket future-alpha support, no restart advice.
